html:
Natal was a British colony on the east coast of South Africa, between the Drakensberg and the Indian Ocean, from 1843 to 1910. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900. Its port was Durban.

Voortrekkers of the Great Trek founded a republic here in 1839, after defeating the Zulu kingdom at Blood River. Britain annexed it in 1843, and most of the Boers moved on to the high veld.

Settlers from Britain built sugar plantations on the coast. From 1860 they brought indentured workers from India to cut the cane, and many stayed. The young lawyer Mohandas Gandhi arrived in 1893 and began his first campaigns against racial laws here.

Natal served as the base for the British invasion of the Zulu kingdom in 1879 and absorbed Zululand in 1897. In the Second Boer War the Boers besieged Ladysmith. In 1910 Natal joined the Union of South Africa.
